what_its_for: Safinamide is used to treat Parkinson's disease. It is added to your levodopa/carbidopa medicine when your symptoms are not fully controlled. It helps reduce the 'off' periods — the times of day when your Parkinson's symptoms like stiffness, tremor, and slow movement come back between doses of your other Parkinson's medicine.
how_to_take: Take safinamide by mouth once a day, at the same time every day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet. Keep taking all your other Parkinson's medicines exactly as prescribed unless your doctor tells you to change them.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 50 mg once daily. After 2 weeks, your doctor may increase your dose to 100 mg once daily if you need better symptom control and you are tolerating the medicine well. Your doctor will decide the right dose for you — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store safinamide at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from moisture, heat, and direct light. Keep the bottle tightly closed. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid foods that are very high in tyramine (such as aged cheeses, cured or fermented meats, sauerkraut, soy sauce, tap beer, and draft beer) because combining safinamide with large amounts of tyramine can cause a dangerous rise in blood pressure. Do not take other MAO inhibitors (such as selegiline, rasagiline, phenelzine, or linezolid) while taking safinamide — this combination can be life-threatening. Avoid St. John's Wort herbal supplements. Be careful when driving or operating machinery, especially until you know how this medicine affects you, since it can cause dizziness or sudden sleepiness. Avoid standing up too quickly, as this medicine can lower blood pressure when you change positions.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: a sudden severe headache, stiff neck, fast or pounding heartbeat, sweating, nausea, or vision changes (these could be signs of very high blood pressure); thoughts of suicide or self-harm; new or worsening confusion, hallucinations, or seeing/hearing things that are not there; uncontrolled movements of the face, arms, or legs; unusual strong urges you cannot control (such as urge to gamble, eat, shop, or have sex); sudden daytime sleepiness or falling asleep without warning; or severe skin reactions with rash, blistering, or peeling.
when_it_works: Some people notice improvement in their 'off' time and smoother movement within a few days to a couple of weeks. However, it may take up to 2 weeks at your full dose to feel the most benefit. Keep taking this medicine every day even if you do not notice changes right away. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Liver problems: If you have moderate or severe liver disease, your dose may need to be lower or this medicine may not be right for you. Tell your doctor about any liver problems before starting. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: It is not known if safinamide is safe during pregnancy or while breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Older adults: Older patients can take this medicine but should be watched carefully for dizziness, falls, and confusion. Children: Safinamide is not approved for use in children.
